transcript.content: Hi, welcome in — I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I came in today because... I've been having this issue at night. Once I start eating, usually when I'm alone, it feels like something just takes over. I really can't stop. Even while I'm sitting there telling myself to put the food away, I just keep going.

After one of these episodes where you feel you can't stop eating, do you ever try to get rid of the food afterward—like making yourself vomit, using laxatives, fasting, or exercising a lot to make up for it?

Yeah, I do. Um... after I eat like that, I usually end up going to the bathroom and making myself throw up. It just feels like the only way to undo it, you know? Like I have to get rid of it before the calories actually settle in.
Over the past few months, about how many times per week have you had these episodes of feeling out of control with eating followed by making yourself vomit?

Um, I'd say for at least the last four months. It's usually been... well, there's usually at least one night each week where I end up eating way more than I meant to when I'm alone, and then I make myself throw up afterward.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports recurrent episodes of eating large amounts of food with a subjective sense of loss of control, occurring at least weekly for over 3 months, followed by compensatory self-induced vomiting to prevent weight gain, consistent with Bulimia Nervosa (F50.2). No mention of significantly low body weight, which would suggest anorexia nervosa binge-purge subtype (F50.01) instead.
